jobs.title: Program Manager, Member Acquisition
jobs.description:
1. About Our Client:
The organization operates in the digital health industry, focusing on metabolic health challenges such as type 2 diabetes and obesity. It addresses these issues by applying AI Digital Twin technology to create personalized metabolic models based on diverse health data. This approach enables members to improve health outcomes including lowering A1C levels, achieving weight loss, and reducing medication use. The organization is experiencing rapid growth and has secured significant funding to expand its impact globally.

2. About the Opportunity:
The Program Manager, Member Acquisition serves as the operational coordinator for the member acquisition function. This role ensures efficient execution of marketing campaigns across multiple channels to attract eligible members to the program. It is central to maintaining campaign schedules, quality, and coordination among cross-functional teams, directly supporting the organization''s growth and member engagement goals.

3. Responsibilities:
• Manage and maintain a consolidated campaign calendar for all member acquisition efforts across various channels.
• Oversee campaign execution including intake, timelines, quality assurance, and approvals.
• Liaise with the MarTech team to manage technical campaign operations and ensure accurate audience targeting and personalization.
• Coordinate with Marketing Operations to ensure timely content delivery and quality compliance.
• Facilitate weekly team meetings and track cross-functional commitments.
• Maintain process documentation and playbooks to preserve institutional knowledge.
• Manage direct mail production timelines and vendor coordination.
• Monitor campaign performance metrics and prepare reports for leadership.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

4. Requirements:
• 2 to 4 years of experience in program management, marketing operations, or similar roles.
• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
• Effective cross-functional communication skills.
• Experience with project management tools, preferably Jira.
• Understanding of marketing campaign operations across email, direct mail, paid digital, or SMS channels.
• Ability to interpret performance data and communicate insights.
• Proactive approach to identifying and resolving issues.
• Experience in health tech or digital health preferred but not required.
• Authorized to work in the U.S.; no visa sponsorship available.

5. Pay Range and Compensation Package:
• The compensation range for this position is $100,000 - $115,000 annually.

jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY:The Program Manager will be responsible for the development, management, and promotion of pickleball programs; the organizing and scheduling of all programming including clinics, leagues, camps, open play, and tournaments. This position reports directly to the General Manager at Jacksonville location.

TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Organize, schedule, administer and promote leagues, round robins, drop-in/open-play, ladders, social events, tournaments, lessons and all other pickleball programming.
Responsible for all club and pickleball activity programming, including developing and promoting pickleball programs for all age groups.

Organize, schedule, and manage daily operation of 5-6 leagues/quarter or more.

Manage and monitor court schedules to maximize usage.
Promote club memberships to all potential prospects.
Responsible for the supervision of the pickleball teaching professionals and coaches including scheduling pickleball clinics and private lessons.

Initiate and execute the selection, hiring, coaching, mentoring, and educating of all pickleball personnel in a manner that reinforces the club’s values and philosophies and ensures the operation of the departments meet company standards.

Post regularly to the Jacksonville PickleRage social media accounts, including updates to programming or events, livestreaming championship matches, and other imagery/posts highlighting play at the facility.

Ability to regularly work during operational hours including evenings, weekends, and select holidays.

Must ensure on-call availability to respond to issues related to pickleball programs.

Ensure that the environment is safe for all those who use the facility.

Adhere to all the various companies, club and department written mandatory standards of operations, policies and procedures, manuals, memos, oral instructions, etc., all of which go to make up the essential functions of the job.

Be an integral part of the management team.

Conduct quarterly meetings with teaching professionals/coaches and club staff.

Implement and stay current with new teaching techniques and receive certifications.

Perform other duties as assigned.

4-year college degree preferred.
Experience in a position such as Pro, Head Pro, Manager, or have served in an Assistant Director or Director position for pickleball, tennis, or other racquet sports or equivalent position
Teaching certifications from PPR or equivalent is a plus
Excellent communication skills including oral, written, and listening
Ability to motivate, organize and lead others
Court Reserve knowledge and experience a plus
Experience creating, organizing, and executing leagues, tournaments, and sport related programming
Outgoing personality and the ability to create and maintain a positive environment through interaction and communication with members, guests, and staff
Proficiency in posting on social media platforms including Facebook and Instagram
Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and holidays pursuant with industry demand

jobs.title: Sr. Data Analyst/ Family Court Program Evaluator (2026-04)
jobs.description:
Senior Program Evaluator / Data Analyst — Family Treatment Court Outcomes Study
We are looking for an expert Data Analyst who can also perform Business and Systems Analysis. This is remote work, about 600-ish hours over 18 months, with opportunity to extend and grow the work over another year.

There are two major portions of the work: business methods/process, cost feasibility, HIPAA/42 CFR Part 2 credibility analysis; and separately dashboards, data stories, accessibility compliance analysis.

This is meaningful, high-visibility work at the intersection of courts, child welfare, and behavioral health — with a small, well-defined dataset, a collaborative multidisciplinary client team, and a mandate to build reporting tools the program can sustain after the engagement ends.

What You'll Do

Lead the analysis of multi-source program data (court records, treatment history, drug testing, placement and permanency data, service referrals, hearing attendance) for a cohort of approximately 25–39 families
Build a data inventory, identify gaps and quality issues, and design practical, repeatable data collection and reporting workflows the court can maintain independently
Conduct descriptive analysis — and inferential or comparative analysis where methodologically defensible given small sample sizes — with honest, well-documented limitations
Assess the feasibility of a full or partial cost analysis (cost avoidance, ROI, or partial cost approaches) and, if approved, design and execute the methodology
Collect qualitative input from program families to fill data gaps, using trauma-informed practices
Produce analysis reports, dashboards, reporting templates, and narrative "data stories" that non-technical audiences — judges, caseworkers, CASA volunteers, treatment providers, funders — can actually use
Present findings to program Steering and Oversight teams twice per year and provide ongoing consultation and office hours to the Statewide FTC Coordinator
Deliver a complete handover package (data dictionaries, methodology documentation, editable templates, workflow instructions) at contract close

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience analyzing sensitive program data in courts, child welfare, behavioral health, substance use treatment, public health, or human services
Working knowledge of HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, and secure handling of confidential data (encryption, role-based access, de-identification)
Demonstrated experience working with small, incomplete, multi-source datasets — and communicating limitations responsibly
Strong data visualization and reporting skills; ability to build dashboards, templates, and infographics in accessible, editable formats
Excellent plain-language writing; a portfolio including reports, visualizations, slide decks, or data stories for non-technical audiences
Proficiency with statistical/analytical tools (R, Python, Stata, SPSS, or equivalent) and visualization/reporting platforms (Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or equivalent)
Experience managing deliverable-driven projects with multiple stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

Prior evaluation of Family Treatment Courts, drug courts, recovery courts, or other multidisciplinary treatment court programs
Experience with judicial branch, DCYF/child welfare agency, CASA, or grant-funded program data
Experience conducting cost analysis, cost avoidance, or ROI studies for public-sector or human services programs
Familiarity with federal grant reporting (OJP/OJJDP performance measures a plus)
Section 508 / WCAG accessibility knowledge for deliverables
Experience supporting continuous quality improvement and sustainability planning

To Apply:

Submit your resume, and 2-3 work samples from similar projects that demonstrate your abilities such as reports, dashboards, data visualizations, or data stories.
